items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: Billy Watrous I think just moved back to L.A. Carl Fontana, Frank Rosolino before he died, all those guys, all the L.A. guys. We see each other occasionally at jazz festivals

ctx.x: And I don’t know if that’s happening now. I don’t want to sound old-fashioned, but—

Well first of all there were many more musicians, there were more jobs so therefore there were more musicians. There aren’t that many musicians anymore. Not that many jobs. I feel badly for kids in school here. I’m sure every once in a while someone’s going to come up and really turn out to be a player of one kind or another. I don’t know where the hell he’s going to work. I mean it used to be you can go to a night club, which is a job, you know, to support a family. But not anymore, unless you go to Vegas or a…
So the idea of jazz education in a sense is wonderful but in another sense it’s like I don’t know where they’re going to go with this education except to educate more people.
